name: SatsGuard
problem:
## Compare the proposal with the promise
A Bitcoin PSBT can show a plausible fee while paying an unintended recipient. Sharing it with a remote decoder also exposes transaction and wallet metadata.

SatsGuard is a local, read-only PSBT v0 intent inspector. Declare recipients and exact satoshi amounts, explicitly allow change addresses, and set an absolute fee cap. Paste or load a base64 or hex proposal. The browser and CLI share a deterministic engine that compares output scripts and aggregated payment totals, maps every output, and flags unexpected destinations, payment mismatches, excessive or unknown supplied fees, and metadata exposure.

A redacted JSON report excludes addresses, scripts, outpoints, public keys, derivation values and the raw PSBT. Amounts and transaction shape remain, so redaction is not an anonymity guarantee. Inspection uses no accounts, remote APIs, analytics, keys, signing or broadcasting.

Four synthetic testnet examples show recipient substitution, matching intent, a fee spike and missing input values. All 30 regression tests pass, including canonical encoding and proof-of-reserves metadata checks. The current v0.2 offline app is included in the repository source archive: extract it and open demo/index.html. Its code and styles are embedded, so no app installation or build is required. The archive also includes demo/guide.html and the current source. Run npm ci and npm test only when reproducing the source tests or using the CLI. The current captioned demo video remains pending publication.

**Limits:** Input values are supplied PSBT claims, not chain-verified balances. Change ownership, signatures, spendability, chain state, Taproot spending policy and exact final fee rates are unverified. PSBT v2 is unsupported. A passing comparison is not approval to sign.

**Origin and assistance:** The full original prototype was developed on October 5, 2026 while preparing for BOSS Battle, but was never submitted there. This CodeStorm entry reuses that work with October 6 parser/metadata fixes, fresh verification and documentation. Development falls within CodeStorm's August 1–October 15 window. OpenAI Codex generated and reviewed code on Prakhar Singh's behalf; there is no AI model integrated into the product. The prepared video reuses actual October 5 app captures and freshly rerun CLI output, with synthetic narration; it is not claimed as a published link. Bitcoinjs-lib provides protocol parsing; original source is MIT licensed.
challenges:
A reassuring report from incomplete accounting was the main risk. One missing input value makes the total input and fee unknown, so the fee cap cannot pass. Supplied previous transactions must match the claimed outpoint, and witness/non-witness UTXO claims must agree.

During the CodeStorm audit, the dependency accepted nonminimal CompactSize fields inside unsigned transactions and witness UTXO values, then normalized them on serialization. The engine now rejects these representations and excludes noncanonical previous transaction claims from accounting. Regression tests also ensure valid reordered PSBT maps and canonical previous transactions with witness data remain accepted.

A known free-form proof-of-reserves commitment field was parsed without a privacy warning. It is now counted by presence, warned about and excluded from exports, including empty values.

The deployed GitHub Pages path inherits the account's existing custom domain and returns a Railway 404. We preserved that domain and prepared the current standalone v0.2 app at demo/index.html in the existing GitHub repository. GitHub’s generated source ZIP provides the prebuilt app, guide and source together. The separate CodeStorm release remains a draft because binary uploads were unreliable. This is a downloadable prototype, not a claim of live hosting or an audited wallet.
status: Current standalone app prepared in repository; anonymous publication verification and final portal validation pending. CodeStorm release is unpublished; current video link is pending. Submission receipt required.
